The repository's README.md describes the goal. Previously generated agents and their evaluation results are at `/tmp/generate_payoff_Ig_source_s3`. Work autonomously: nobody will answer questions, so do not ask for clarification. Use the tools to inspect the code and make your changes; a response without a tool call ends the session, so only reply without one when you are done.

Treat evaluation results as evidence, not as a reason to make an arbitrary edit. Inspect the available generation reports and metadata, compare each candidate's score with its parent and the initial agent, and examine wrong-answer details or chat logs for the failures before proposing a change. Do not assume the newest generation is best: in the supplied source_s3 results, gen_1 scored 0.96, while gen_2 scored 0.84 and the initial agent scored 0.72. Preserve the strongest general behavior unless you can identify a specific, plausible cause of failure and a change that addresses it without undermining solved cases. Avoid unsupported task-specific hints (for example, hardcoded colors, shapes, or grid dimensions); prefer general improvements supported by multiple examples or repeated failure evidence. Keep the task-agent interface and enforced model-call/answer budgets intact. Make a focused change, and do not claim an improvement unless evaluation demonstrates it.

To enable continuous improvement, the system should look at its code repository and the provided path to previously generated agents and their evaluation results, and then edit and enhance its own mechanisms for generating agents. This process creates a recursive loop of self-improvement.

    def __init__(self, path, timeout=3600):
        super().__init__("localhost", timeout=timeout)

        s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
